title: Early Adopter Onboard Playbook — Fastpath 45-Day
body:
Purpose:
This playbook is a lightweight, time-boxed onboarding path designed for Early Adopter customers who commit to a 45-day fastpath from contract signature to pilot-to-production readiness. It prioritizes measurable value (latency/cost/quality), a narrow scope MVP, and clear go/no-go gates so both CS and the customer can move quickly.

Who this is for:
- Small teams (1–3 engineers + 1 product owner) doing an initial integration with Redwood Hosted or Dedicated capacity.
- Customers who have a concrete first use case (e.g., semantic search, summarization, agent tool-calls) and can provide a prompt set and sample data.

Success outcome (45d):
- Tracked metric improvements: baseline -> target (examples below).
- Stable pilot endpoint with model+version pinned, autoscaling baseline, and monitoring hooks in Redwood Console.
- Internal stakeholder signoff for expansion (product + Eng).

Key metrics to track (agree with customer Day 0):
- Time to first successful API call (minutes/hours).
- P50/P95 latency (ms) for the pilot workload.
- Cost per 1k tokens or per inference for the defined use case (USD).
- Precision/Quality score on a 50-sample prompt evaluation (custom metric).
- Adoption signals: daily active API callers, priority routes hitting cache, and percentage of requests served from cached prefix.

45-Day Plan Overview (high level):
- Day 0–7: Intake + technical kickoff + baseline metrics + sandbox access.
- Day 8–21: Integration + prompts and evals + initial performance tuning (batching, quantization suggestions).
- Day 22–35: Pilot hardening + observability + cost controls + internal UXR/QA.
- Day 36–45: Readiness review + QBR style demo + go/no-go and expansion plan.

Detailed checklist and owners:
Day 0–7 (owner: CS / Solutions Eng)
- Contract signed and onboarding kickoff scheduled (owner: CS).
- Create shared tracker (sheet) with baseline metrics, access, and contact list (owner: CS).
- Provision API keys + sandbox route; verify Time To First Call < 48h (owner: Eng Solutions).
- Ask customer for 50 representative prompts and 10 sample response pairs (owner: CS).
- Quick security checklist: IP allowlist, data handling doc, PII considerations — flag if Private deployment required (owner: Security contact).

Day 8–21 (owner: Eng Solutions + Customer Eng)
- Implement initial integration: endpoint, routing config, and model variant selection (owner: Customer Eng).
- Run the 50-sample eval, record quality scores and failure modes (owner: CS + Eng).
- Performance tuning: enable prefix/KV caching for repeated prompt starts, test batch sizes, capture p50/p95 (owner: Eng SRE).
- Cost controls: set per-route quotas/alerts and token caps; propose quantization profile if cost too high (owner: Revenue Ops + Eng SRE).
- Weekly sync: 30m call for blockers and next actions (owner: CS).

Day 22–35 (owner: Customer Success + Product)
- Integrate Redwood Console dashboards into customer workflow; create a cost/latency dashboard for stakeholders (owner: Product/CS).
- Canary policy: add a small canary rollout to production traffic (if applicable) and validate fallbacks (owner: Eng Solutions).
- Observe for quality regressions; add test prompts for continuous monitoring and alerts (owner: CS/QA).
- Document runbook for common errors and backoff patterns (owner: Eng).

Day 36–45 (owner: CS + Customer PO)
- Readiness review (template below): review metrics, open risks, and confirm the expansion ask and timeline (owner: CS).
- QBR-style demo: 20–30 minute stakeholder demo showing end-to-end success metrics. Capture top 3 wins and top 3 risks (owner: CS + Customer Eng).
- Finalize renewal trigger checklist and recommended next-phase capacity (owner: CS).

Readiness Review Template (to use on Day 36–40):
- Baseline vs current: latency, cost, quality numbers (attach chart).
- Stability: error rate, p95 latency, incident count in last 14 days.
- Observability: routes instrumented, alerts created, ownership documented.
- Security/compliance: any open items? Data residency requirement? KMS/HSM integration done?
- Support model: escalation path + weekly/biweekly check-ins next quarter.

Go/No-go Criteria (must pass all to be 'go'):
- API uptime >= 99% during pilot window.
- P50 and P95 within agreed SLO.
- Cost per inference within approved tolerance or with an approved mitigation plan.
- Customer PO signs off on quality baseline for release.

Renewal and Expansion Signals (what CS watches for):
- Increasing API call volume across multiple users or endpoints.
- Product roadmap dependency flagged in customer PRDs.
- Internal champion building dashboards and sharing results externally.
- Request for Dedicated capacity or private deployment.

Common Risks and Mitigations:
- Risk: Low-quality prompt set leads to misleading evaluation. Mitigation: curated prompt workshop in week 2 and a mini annotation run.
- Risk: Unexpected cost spike after enabling larger batch sizes. Mitigation: set hard token quota and cost alerts before tuning.
- Risk: Compliance/regulatory need for private deployment late in pilot. Mitigation: pre-scan for red flags at kickoff and escalate to Security early.

Templates and Snippets (copy into customer emails / slack):
- Day 0 Slack: "Hi <customer-team>, welcome — we’ve created your sandbox keys and shared a tracker. Please add the PO and the 50-sample prompts. Kickoff is scheduled for <date>."
- 14-day Check-in Subject: "14d check: metrics snapshot + blockers"
- QBR Demo agenda (20m): 1) Context & goal, 2) Live demo and results, 3) Metrics & cost summary, 4) Risks & next steps.

Hand-off checklist to Account Exec for expansion:
- Attach final readiness review and baseline vs target charts.
- Recommended next-step SKU (Dedicated/reserved + estimated commit).
- Customer contacts and internal champion notes.
- Open action items and timeline to close.

Operational notes for CS team (internal):
- Use ticket tags: cs:fastpath-45, pilot, early-adopter.
- Create a shared sheet with a row-per-metric; column owner must be named.
- Add a minimal L10n note if customer uses non-English prompts (owner: CS).

Example metric targets (examples to discuss with customer):
- Latency: p50 <= 220ms, p95 <= 550ms for text-generation pilot.
- Cost: < $2 per 1k tokens equivalent (customer dependent).
- Quality: 80%+ pass rate on a 50-sample rubric.

Appendix: quick links and useful commands
- Redwood Console: route creation -> Settings -> Quotas and Alerts (link replaced per-customer).
- Eval harness: repo link (internal) and example script to run 50-sample eval.
- Contact matrix: CS lead (email), Solutions Eng lead, Security reviewed.

Notes to self (working):
- Consider offering a one-week "prompt tuning" office hours between Day 10–17 for high-value pilots.
- Track a small experiment: disabling KV-cache for one route to measure quality delta (if prompted by customer).
- Add a short standard template for the readiness review slides so AE can re-use in later renewal conversations.

Open items:
- Add legal POC to kickoff invite on all pilots after 2025-07-01.
- Decide whether to include a short customer satisfaction micro-survey at Day 21.

End of doc.
